t.1.106.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With Dhṛtarāṣṭra's permission, he presented the wealth won by his own arms to Bhīṣma, to Satyavatī, and to his mother.
t.1.106.2: And Pāṇḍu sent that wealth to Vidura as well, and the righteous-souled one also gratified his friends with wealth.
t.1.106.4: His mother Kausalyā rejoiced as she embraced that bull among men of matchless splendour, as Paulomī embraces Jayanta.
t.1.106.3: Then, O Bhārata, Bhīṣma gladdened Satyavatī and the illustrious Kausalyā with the splendid jewels won by Pāṇḍu.
t.1.106.6: And then, O bull of the Bharatas, Pāṇḍu, united with Kuntī and with Mādrī and having conquered weariness, became a dweller in the forest.
t.1.106.5: Through the valiant conquests of that hero, Dhṛtarāṣṭra performed a hundred horse sacrifices, great rites with sacrificial fees of a hundred thousand.
t.1.106.7: Abandoning his palace dwelling and his splendid beds, he lived constantly in the forest, ever devoted to the hunt.
t.1.106.8: Wandering over the lovely southern flank of the Himavat mountain, he dwelt upon the mountain ridges and in the forests of great śāla trees.
t.1.106.9: Pāṇḍu, dwelling in the forest together with Kuntī and Mādrī, shone like Puraṃdara's glorious elephant standing between two she-elephants.
t.1.106.10: As the Bhārata king roamed with his two wives, bearing arrows, sword and bow, clad in bright armour, a hero versed in the supreme weapons, the forest-dwellers thought of him, "This is a god."
t.1.106.11: Urged on by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, men tirelessly and constantly brought him the objects of his desire and all manner of enjoyments in the depths of the forests.
t.1.106.13: Then the bull among men, having chosen her and had her brought, caused the marriage of the great-minded Vidura to be performed.
t.1.106.14: And on her Vidura, the joy of the Kurus, begot sons endowed with discipline, like himself in their virtues.
t.1.106.12: Then the son of the river heard of a maiden endowed with beauty and youth, the Pāraśava daughter of King Devaka.
